questions.question: The OSI model has how many layers, bottom to top?
options: 7 — Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application

questions.question: OSI Layer 1 (Physical) is concerned with:
options: Bits on the wire/fiber/radio — signaling, connectors, media, raw transmission

questions.question: OSI Layer 2 (Data Link) typically handles:
options: Framing, MAC addressing, switching/bridging within a broadcast domain

questions.question: OSI Layer 3 (Network) is where you primarily find:
options: Logical addressing and routing (IP, routers/L3 switches, FIB lookups)

questions.question: OSI Layer 4 (Transport) is best associated with:
options: End-to-end delivery semantics — e.g. TCP reliability/ports or UDP datagrams

questions.question: OSI Layers 5–7 (Session, Presentation, Application) roughly cover:
options: Dialog/session control, data representation/encoding, and end-user network applications/protocols
questions.explanation: Upper layers — often collapsed in TCP/IP mental models.

questions.question: How does the practical TCP/IP model relate to OSI?
options: TCP/IP collapses some OSI layers (e.g. L5–L7 into Application; Link often covers L1–L2) but the OSI names still help locate faults
TCP/IP has 7 identical layers with the same names
OSI replaced TCP/IP on the internet
questions.explanation: Interviewers want mapping literacy, not pedantry.

questions.question: A useful OSI troubleshooting habit is:
options: Start from symptoms and test bottom-up or top-down systematically (L1 link → L2/L3 reachability → L4 ports → app)
Only ever look at Layer 7 first and stop
Ignore Physical because bits never fail
Skip L3 if ping works once

questions.question: An L2 switch vs L3 router/switch in OSI terms:
options: L2 switch forwards on MAC (Data Link); L3 device routes on IP (Network)—many 'L3 switches' do both in ASICs
L3 devices cannot have Ethernet ports

questions.question: In 'life of a packet' terms, crossing a router hop mainly exercises which OSI layers?
options: L3 decision (IP/FIB) plus L2 rewrite toward the next hop on the egress media (and L1 on the wire)
Only Layer 7 HTTP parsing on every hop
Only Presentation ASN.1 on the spine
questions.explanation: Tie OSI to fabric packet flow.

questions.question: Encapsulation moving down the OSI stack means:
options: Higher-layer PDUs get headers (and sometimes trailers) from lower layers — e.g. TCP segment in IP packet in Ethernet frame
Only compressing with gzip at L1
questions.explanation: PDU nesting is core OSI literacy.

questions.question: Which mapping is most accurate?
options: Ethernet/MAC ≈ L2; IP/ICMP ≈ L3; TCP/UDP ≈ L4; HTTP/DNS/TLS≈ upper layers (L5–L7 in OSI terms)
